data.title: PHINIA appoints Treasurer Gordon Muir as CFO
data.description:
PHINIA (PHIN) announced Friday the appointment of Gordon Muir as senior vice president and chief financial officer, effective January 1, 2027.

The company noted that Muir succeeds Chris Gropp, current SVP and CFO, who will retire, effective March 31, 2027.

Gropp will support the transition period starting January 1 through March 31, 2027, as Special Advisor, also reporting to Brady Ericson, president and chief executive officer, focusing on a smooth and well-coordinated transition of responsibilities.

The company noted that Gordon joined BorgWarner in 2007 and has been part of PHINIA since its spin-off in 2023. He currently serves as PHINIA's treasurer, with responsibility for treasury and investor relations, and has played a key role in the company's financial strategy and capital markets activities. 

Source: press release

data.title: Procter & Gamble plans to use AI and automation to free up cash
data.description:
Procter & Gamble (PG) is in the spotlight after the consumer products giant unveiled a renewed cost savings program during its Investor Day event on Thursday. Notably, the Cincinnati-based company committed to a total of another $10B in cost savings in four years through FY30, mostly focused on using AI capabilities to accelerate speed of execution to deliver higher consumer usage and solve consumer problems. A 20% to 30% reduction in product supply workforce (including contractors) and increased use of automation will also factor in.

Following the initiatives, Procter & Gamble (PG) plans to reinvest the extra savings in growth while assuming roughly flat headcount and media spending.

During a Q&A session, CFO Andre Schulten reiterated that the main focus is to reinvest in the business to create the volume and scale that leads to higher margins. "We think this is the right approach given the opportunity to tap in more value-conscious consumers who can then uptrade when disposable income improves," noted JPMorgan analyst Andrea Texeira on the update. "We came away confident that PG can count on its strong moats of digital capabilities, supply chain efficiency, and R&D leadership that should continue to reaccelerate the growth to tackle the remaining 21 out of 50 category/country combinations in which P&G needs to improve share," added Texiera. 

JPMorgan kept its Overweight rating on Procter & Gamble (PG) in place.

Shares of Procter & Gamble (PG) moved 1.3% higher in premarket trading to $169.98. The 52-week high is $173.59.

data.title: Nvidia, AMD in focus as GF Securities says talk of server CPU cuts is 'overstated'
data.description:
Despite rumors that tech companies have started to cut orders for server CPUs, GF Securities said supply chain checks show just the opposite.

The Hong Kong-based investment firm said any talk that Meta (META) and Microsoft (MSFT) have cut orders is inaccurate and that Meta has shifted some purchases of x86 to Nvidia's (NVDA) Grace and Vera server options. Additionally, Meta has accelerated general-server deployments for its Muse artificial intelligence agent.

For Microsoft, orders are unchanged, and any noise is simply reflecting original design manufacturer capacity allocations. 

“Agentic workloads now account for ~80% of tokens on OpenRouter (weekly volume up 35x YoY), with GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol and Claude Duet supporting commercial adoption, while Meta Muse gained 11.2mn NA accounts in 7 weeks but saw Day-30 retention fall to 16.4%,” analysts at the firm wrote in a note to clients. “We maintain server CPU TAM of $211bn by 2030 (+47% CAGR), with 2027 unit growth of 29% (general servers +15%, AI-inference CPUs +79%) as agentic AI expands from 25% to 50% of total inference.”

The investment firm reiterated its Buy rating on AMD as it sees the Dr. Lisa Su-led company benefiting from a ramp in its Venice CPUs and continued share gains in x86 processors.

“We expect Venice to drive further share gains for AMD in the coming quarters, even outperforming Intel’s Diamond Rapids (set to launch by late 1Q27), on the back of superior perf-per-watt, large L3 SRAM, and up to 512 threads,” analysts at the firm added. “For now, we forecast Venice CPU shipments of 400k/5.4mn in 2026/2027, respectively.”

The firm also reiterated its Buy rating on Intel due to the company ramping up its Granite Rapids processors.

data.title: MasTec to acquire mechanical contractor Murphy for about $1.25B
data.description:
MasTec (MTZ) on Friday said it will acquire mechanical contractor Murphy for roughly $1.25 billion in cash.

The company said the deal will boost MasTec’s business in mission-critical infrastructure markets, including aviation and defense, pharmaceutical, healthcare, technology, and advanced manufacturing.

“Murphy expands MasTec’s capabilities in some of the fastest-growing and most diverse infrastructure markets in North America. Its highly skilled union craft workforce, supported by established apprenticeship, training and field-leadership programs, provides the labor capacity and execution expertise required to deliver large, complex projects safely and efficiently,” said MasTec’s Chief Executive Officer Jose Mas.

Murphy will serve as a new operating group of MasTec, and Murphy’s financial results are expected to be reflected in the Clean Energy and Infrastructure Segment, MasTec said. Murphy's management team, led by President and Chief Executive Officer Patrick Murphy, will remain in place following the transaction.

MasTec said there is a potential earnout payment based on the cumulative three-year financial performance of Murphy post-closing.

Murphy is projected to generate full calendar year 2026 revenue and an adjusted EBITDA of about $775 million and roughly $140 million, respectively, it added.

Shares of MasTec, which is an infrastructure engineering and construction company, were down over 1% in premarket trading.

data.title: Union Pacific powers past controversy in its bid to merge with Norfolk Southern
data.description:
Union Pacific (UNP) and Norfolk Southern (NSC) filed a response to Canadian Pacific Kansas City's (CPKC) request that the Surface Transportation Board terminate review of the merger application for a transcontinental railroad.

On October 30, rival Class I railroad Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC) seized on the old remarks made by Union Pacific (UNP) CEO Jim Vena on raising rates to certain customers to "teach you a lesson"  to aggressively challenge the merger review process. Union Pacific (UNP) clarified that it "does not retaliate against customers" and insisted a shipper's stance on the merger would never affect its rates or service.

Union Pacific (UNP) and Norfolk Southern (NSC) noted that they remain focused on advancing a transaction that will give U.S. businesses more options to compete in the global marketplace, lower transportation costs, and protect tens-of-thousands of union jobs. The companies said they look forward to the Surface Transportation Board continued evaluation of the proposed combination based on the facts, evidence, and public interest benefits presented in the record. 

Written public comments on the proposed merger closed on November 18, and preliminary comments from the Department of Justice and the Department of Transportation are due on December 3. Union Pacific (UNP) and Norfolk Southern (NSC) must submit their responses to these comments by February 16, 2027, followed by a public STB hearing scheduled to take place after March 29, 2027. Final briefs are due on May 28, 2027, after which the evidentiary record will close. The STB is expected to issue its final decision within 90 days of the record closing, targeting final approval and transaction completion by late summer 2027.

data.title: Equinor says cyberattack against it has been stopped
data.description:
Equinor (EQNR) said Friday that the cyberattack against it has been stopped with no ⁠impact to production ​and no ​indication data had been stolen or altered.

Europe's largest gas ​supplier had detected the attack three days ago but said it was not a virus attack, so there was no chance of it spreading, and that it also did not appear to be specifically targeting the company.

At least two Norwegian energy companies reported a cyberattack or an attempted attack at around the same time this week.

"There is also no indication that the attack has had any negative consequences for employees, partners, or suppliers," Equinor (EQNR) said.

data.title: Netease outlines Ananta global launch on January 15, 2027 as Q3 online games revenue declines sequentially
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: NetEase (NTES) Q3 2026

Management View

  • NetEase reported RMB 27.9 billion of total net revenues in Q3, with games and related value-added services contributing RMB 22.9 billion, while emphasizing long-life live operations across established franchises and new releases. Bill Pang said the company is “advancing a diverse pipeline of original concepts across genres and themes,” while continuing to “invigorate our established games with new content and gameplay mechanics.”

  • Management highlighted engagement spikes and chart performance across several franchises, including Onmyoji’s 10th anniversary. Bill Pang said “monthly active users reached their highest level since 2022, and the game hit #3 on China's iOS top grossing chart following the anniversary update.”

  • On global traction, Bill Pang said “Where Winds Meet continues to demonstrate the global traction of our high-quality game content” and added that “its player base surpassed 100 million worldwide in August.”

  • NetEase positioned Marvel Rivals as a key global live-ops title. Bill Pang said the “Krakoan Reels Volume 2 update released on August 13 propelled the game to #1 on Steam's Top Sellers chart, both globally and in the United States,” and noted the esports program’s grand finals are “set to take place in Stockholm in late November.”

  • NetEase disclosed a specific launch timeline for a major pipeline game. Bill Pang said “Ananta, our urban open-world title, is currently slated for a global launch on January 15, 2027, across PC, PlayStation 5 and mobile platforms.”

  • Aileen Bin Mo summarized profitability and capital return items, including, “our non-GAAP net income attributable to shareholders for the third quarter totaled RMB 9.2 billion,” and “our Board of Directors has approved a dividend of USD 0.117 per share, or USD 0.585 per ADS for the third quarter.”

Outlook

  • NetEase did not provide explicit revenue or EPS guidance ranges in the prepared remarks or Q&A in this transcript; management instead framed near-term execution around live operations, content cadence, and the Ananta launch timeline.

  • On Ananta’s commercial model and long-term revenue framing, Zhipeng Hu said, “we're more focused on long-term revenue scale than ARPU itself,” adding, “we believe cosmetic-based monetization can actually lower the barrier to experiencing the game content.”

  • For Where Winds Meet, management outlined a forward content and operations cadence. An unnamed executive said the team will “remain a release cadence with one high-quality large-scale map update every year alongside ongoing updates to themed maps, diverse storylines and new martial arts styles.”

Financial Results

  • Aileen Bin Mo reported Q3 total net revenues of RMB 27.9 billion ($4.2 billion) and online games net revenues of RMB 22.4 billion, “compared with RMB 24.5 billion” in the preceding quarter, stating the sequential decline “was primarily due to lower net revenue from certain self-developed games.”

  • Segment trends were mixed: Youdao net revenues were RMB 1.4 billion (vs. RMB 1.5 billion preceding quarter), NetEase Cloud Music net revenues were RMB 1.9 billion (vs. RMB 2 billion preceding quarter), and innovative businesses and others were RMB 1.5 billion (vs. RMB 1.6 billion preceding quarter).

  • Margin expanded year-over-year. Aileen Bin Mo said gross profit was RMB 19 billion and gross margin was 68.4%, while games and related VAS gross margin was 74.3%, with the improvement “primarily driven by lower revenue-sharing costs.”

  • Operating cost ratios and capital position were detailed: total operating expenses were RMB 9.6 billion (34.5% of net revenues), and “as of September 30, 2026, our net cash position was RMB 175.2 billion.”

Q&A

  • Yang Liu, Morgan Stanley: asked about Ananta’s cosmetics-driven monetization, long-term revenue setting vs. gacha ARPU, and internal test performance; Zhipeng Hu: said “we're more focused on long-term revenue scale than ARPU itself,” and “we're currently running internal tests and evaluate across various aspects of the game,” with “final refinements to ensure the game hits the quality [ bar ].”

  • Lincoln Kong, Goldman Sachs: asked whether AI-driven short drama growth could pressure gaming time spent and what AI changes in entertainment imply for talent/org capability; CEO William Ding: said “in the short term, there will be an impact on the attention span,” but “in the long term, it will not necessarily impact game that much,” adding “AI really solved for our industry is bring a tremendous amount of efficiency improvement.”

  • Ruzhe Su, Morningstar Inc.: asked about commercialization and pipeline for World of Warcraft: Forever and other Blizzard classics, and about challenges plus upcoming content for Where Winds Meet; Zhipeng Hu: said “World of Warcraft: Forever performed above our expectations,” and that “the purchase of annual pass also set a record,” while adding Overwatch delivered “the best commercial performance since its launch in China”; Unnamed executive: said Where Winds Meet “continued to perform steadily,” and outlined a three-part plan spanning “high-quality content,” “global live operations,” and “long-term goals of our diverse player base.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was neutral to slightly skeptical, pressing on monetization durability (Ananta), competitive attention risk (short drama), and monetization performance/pipeline (Blizzard), as shown by questions about “rather low ARPU” and “competition of time spent.”

  • Management tone was slightly positive and confident on long-term operations and content cadence, with Zhipeng Hu emphasizing “long-term revenue scale,” and the Where Winds Meet team stating they are “fully confident in this long-term value as the established title.”

  • Versus the prior quarter, Q3 carried a more performance-accountability tone around specific titles (e.g., Blizzard commercialization and Where Winds Meet operational challenges), while Q2 emphasized broad product momentum and portfolio strength in prepared remarks.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • NetEase reported Q3 total net revenues of RMB 27.9 billion vs. RMB 30.1 billion in Q2, alongside Q3 online games net revenues of RMB 22.4 billion vs. RMB 24.5 billion in Q2, with Q3 attributing the sequential online-games decline to “lower net revenue from certain self-developed games.”

  • Strategic emphasis shifted from Q2’s focus on new release Sea of Remnants and portfolio-wide growth framing to Q3’s concentration on global-scale milestones and specific pipeline timing, including “surpassed 100 million worldwide” for Where Winds Meet and the Ananta launch date of January 15, 2027.

  • Analyst focus rotated from Q2’s questions on pipeline timing and growth drivers to Q3’s deeper scrutiny of monetization model design (Ananta), time-spend competition (short drama), and tangible commercialization metrics for Blizzard titles.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management flagged near-term revenue pressure drivers in games: Aileen Bin Mo said the sequential decline in online games net revenues “was primarily due to lower net revenue from certain self-developed games.”

  • Attention competition was acknowledged. CEO William Ding said short-form drama growth “does attract a lot of users' attention,” and “in the short term, there will be an impact on the attention span.”

  • Execution risk around Ananta quality was addressed through ongoing testing and refinement. Zhipeng Hu said the team is “making final refinements to ensure the game hits the quality [ bar ].”

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 around sustaining long-life franchises while building global-scale titles and setting clearer pipeline timing, including Ananta’s planned January 15, 2027 global launch. Financially, the company reported lower sequential online games net revenues tied to certain self-developed games, alongside higher year-over-year margin drivers such as lower revenue-sharing costs, and reiterated shareholder returns through a higher quarterly dividend per ADS and continued repurchases under the $5 billion program.

data.title: Which casino operator will win F1 weekend in Las Vegas?
data.description:
The Las Vegas Grand Prix is taking over the Las Vegas Strip this weekend. While the Formula One race creates traffic issues and pedestrian congestion, it is also one of the biggest Strip hotel pricing weekends of the year and attracts international baccarat players. Those are positive developments considering the weekend before Thanksgiving was traditionally one of the slowest periods on the Las Vegas calendar before it was transformed into a high-margin luxury event, injecting over $900M to $1.5B annually into the regional economy.

Analysts have Wynn Resorts (WYNN) circled as the best positioned casino operator to take advantage of the Grand Prix weekend, while MGM Resorts (MGM) is also expected to benefit and Caesars Entertainment (CZR) is seen as facing a more uneven picture. 

A survey by Truist of hotel room rates for November indicated Wynn (WYNN) properties were up 29%, driven higher by VIP guests packaged tied to the Grand Prix weekend. The Truist survey showed MGM's (MGM) room rates are also higher for November rates, while the room rates at Caesars properties (CZR) are notably lower on average due in part to a lower mix of affluent guests. Of note, Caesars (CZR) has eight properties along the track, while MGM's (MGM) Bellagio and Cosmopolitan sit on the course. 

The primary stock directly tied to Formula One racing is the Formula One Group tracking stock, issued by its parent company Liberty Media Corporation and traded on the Nasdaq under the tickers (FWONK) and (FWONA).

data.title: Prospect Capital exits Security Fire Systems with 41.8% realized IRR
data.description:
Prospect Capital (PSEC) achieved a 41.8% realized gross annualized internal rate of return from the completion of the exit of its senior secured first lien term loan and preferred equity investment from Security Fire Systems, it said Friday.

The business development company received cash exit proceeds of ~$25M for its investment in SFS. The exit achieved a 1.2x multiple of invested capital through a combination of interest income, prepayment fees, equity distributions, and other cash flows.

"Our realization of this investment demonstrates our ability to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns by investing in the lower middle market," said Angel Solis, managing director at Prospect (PSEC).

Prospect Capital (PSCC) stock rose 0.8% in premarket trading.

SFS offers a broad line of fire security and protection products and services, including  automatic fire sprinkler design services, fire sprinkler system installation, system testing, system maintenance and servicing, remodel & retrofits, fire alarms, and emergency response.
